claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. It's helpful to know he's 8 years old and lives with you.

I have a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

Are you responsible for Alex's upbringing, such as paying for his food, clothes, and accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after Alex and pay for everything he needs - his food, clothes, and of course he lives here with me at home. I'm his parent and responsible for all his care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. It's great that you're responsible for Alex's care.

Now, could you please tell me about your own situation:

Do you live in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Manchester is lovely!

Just a couple more questions:

Is Alex either a UK resident, or does he normally live with you in the UK? And is he in full-time education, or if he's not in education, is he under 16?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives here with me in the UK - he's at home with me in Manchester. And yes, he's only 8 years old, so he's well under 16 and goes to primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Wonderful, thank you for confirming that.

One more question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Based on what you've told me, I have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me confirm the key details:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- He lives with you in the UK (Manchester)
- You are responsible for his upbringing and pay for his food, clothes, and accommodation
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for him

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

✅ **Alex is under 16** – He's 8 years old, which is well within the age requirement.

✅ **You live in the UK** – You're based in Manchester.

✅ **You're responsible for Alex** – He lives with you and you pay for his food, clothes, and accommodation.

✅ **No one else is claiming** – You're the only person looking after him and claiming for him.

You can apply for Child Benefit online through the government website. If you have any other questions about the application process, feel free to ask!

All core eligibility requirements are satisfied.
